title: Viceroys and Governor-Generals of India: Quiz

questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of India (not merely of Bengal)?
questions.rationale: The Charter Act of 1833 created the post, and Bentinck was its first holder. Hastings was first Governor-General of Bengal and Canning the first Viceroy.

questions.question: The Subsidiary Alliance system is associated with:
questions.rationale: Wellesley (1798 to 1805) used Subsidiary Alliances. Cornwallis is linked with the Permanent Settlement and Dalhousie with the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.question: Sati was declared illegal in 1829 under which Governor-General?
questions.rationale: Bentinck's Regulation XVII of 1829 outlawed sati, helped by the campaign of Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

questions.question: The first passenger railway in India, Bombay to Thane, opened during the term of:
questions.rationale: The line opened on 16 April 1853, in Dalhousie's term. He also began the telegraph and Post Office Act of 1854.

questions.question: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
questions.rationale: Canning became Viceroy in 1858 after the Government of India Act transferred rule to the Crown. Dalhousie was the Governor-General before him.

questions.question: Which Viceroy was assassinated in office in the Andamans in 1872?
questions.rationale: Lord Mayo was stabbed at Port Blair, the only Viceroy killed in office.

questions.question: Which of these is correctly matched with Lord Lytton?
options: Vernacular Press Act and Arms Act of 1878
questions.rationale: Lytton passed the press and arms laws in 1878. The Ilbert Bill belongs to Ripon, the partition to Curzon and the Factory Act to Lansdowne.

questions.question: Who repealed the Vernacular Press Act and promoted local self-government in 1882?
questions.rationale: Ripon repealed the Act in 1882 and issued the resolution on local self-government. Lytton had passed it.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 during the Viceroyalty of:
questions.rationale: Dufferin held office from 1884 to 1888. A.O. Hume helped found the Congress in December 1885.

questions.question: Which statement about Lord Curzon is correct?
options: He founded the Indian National Congress
He annulled the partition of Bengal
He signed the Gandhi pact of 1931
questions.rationale: Curzon's partition took effect in 1905 and was annulled in 1911 under Hardinge II. The 1931 pact was signed by Irwin.

questions.question: The announcement that the capital would shift from Calcutta to Delhi came at the Durbar of 1911 under:
questions.rationale: The 1911 Durbar, with King George V present, announced the shift and annulled the partition of Bengal.

questions.question: Which Viceroy is linked with the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Rowlatt Act?
questions.rationale: Both belong to 1919, when Chelmsford (1916 to 1921) was Viceroy. Reading followed him.

questions.question: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in:
questions.rationale: Gandhi and Irwin signed the pact in March 1931 before the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.question: Which Viceroy served for the longest time, bringing India into the Second World War?
questions.rationale: Linlithgow (1936 to 1943) held office for over seven years and declared India at war in 1939. Wavell came after him.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT correctly paired?
options: Lord Wavell: Quit India Movement of 1942
Lord Minto II: Surat split of 1907
questions.rationale: The Quit India Movement of 1942 came under Linlithgow, since Wavell took over in October 1943. The other pairs are correct.
